hints: Use integration by parts on \(\int_0^1(2-x)e^{-2x}\,dx\), taking \(u=2-x\) and \(dv=e^{-2x}dx\).
Then \(du=-dx\) and \(v=-\tfrac12e^{-2x}\); substitute these into \(uv-\int v\,du\).
Complete the remaining exponential integral before applying the limits \(0\) and \(1\), keeping the result exact.
walkthrough:
State the given definite integral:
$$I = \int_0^1 (2 - x)\mathrm{e}^{-2x}\,dx$$

Apply integration by parts using the formula $\int u\,dv = uv - \int v\,du$:
Choose $u = 2 - x$ (to be differentiated) and $dv = \mathrm{e}^{-2x}\,dx$ (to be integrated).

Substitute $u, v, du$ into the integration by parts formula:
$$\int (2 - x)\mathrm{e}^{-2x}\,dx = (2 - x)\left(-\dfrac{1}{2}\mathrm{e}^{-2x}\right) - \int \left(-\dfrac{1}{2}\mathrm{e}^{-2x}\right)(-dx)$$
$$= -\dfrac{1}{2}(2 - x)\mathrm{e}^{-2x} - \dfrac{1}{2}\int \mathrm{e}^{-2x}\,dx$$

Multiply by the constant factor $-\dfrac{1}{2}$ to find the complete antiderivative $F(x)$:
$$-\dfrac{1}{2}\left(-\dfrac{1}{2}\mathrm{e}^{-2x}\right) = +\dfrac{1}{4}\mathrm{e}^{-2x}$$
$$F(x) = -\dfrac{1}{2}(2 - x)\mathrm{e}^{-2x} + \dfrac{1}{4}\mathrm{e}^{-2x} = \left(-\dfrac{1}{2}(2 - x) + \dfrac{1}{4}\right)\mathrm{e}^{-2x} = \left(-1 + \dfrac{1}{2}x + \dfrac{1}{4}\right)\mathrm{e}^{-2x} = \left(\dfrac{1}{2}x - \dfrac{3}{4}\right)\mathrm{e}^{-2x}$$

Evaluate the antiderivative at the upper limit $x = 1$:
$$F(1) = \left(\dfrac{1}{2}(1) - \dfrac{3}{4}\right)\mathrm{e}^{-2(1)} = \left(\dfrac{2}{4} - \dfrac{3}{4}\right)\mathrm{e}^{-2} = -\dfrac{1}{4}\mathrm{e}^{-2}$$

Evaluate the antiderivative at the lower limit $x = 0$:
$$F(0) = \left(\dfrac{1}{2}(0) - \dfrac{3}{4}\right)\mathrm{e}^{-2(0)} = \left(-\dfrac{3}{4}\right)(1) = -\dfrac{3}{4}$$

Factor out $\dfrac{1}{4}$ to state the exact answer:
$$I = \dfrac{1}{4}\left(3 - \mathrm{e}^{-2}\right)$$

ai_rubric.Integration: Integration begins with $a(2-x)e^{-2x}+b\int e^{-2x}\,dx$, or equivalent. Completes integration and derives $-\frac12(2-x)e^{-2x}+\frac14e^{-2x}$, or equivalent. Concludes with $\frac14(3-e^{-2})$.
